title.narrative: OHCHR främjande av mänskliga rättigheter i Latinamerika 2023-2025
OHCHR promoting human rights in Latin America 2023-2025

description.narrative:
Insatsen avser stöd till FNs Högkommissionär för Mänskliga Rättigheter (OHCHR) och deras regionala projekt för främjande av mänskliga rättigheter i Latinamerika under perioden 2023 till 2025, fokus ligger på tre områden:
1. Främjande av det demokratiska utrymmet och skydd av försvarare av mänskliga rättigheter och journalister.
2. Främjande och skydd av migranters mänskliga rättigheter i sårbara situationer.
3. Främjande av rätten till en ren, hälsosam och hållbar miljö.

Decision on contribution, OHCHR Latin America 2023-2025

description.narrative:
Examples of progress results of the first pillar in 2023:
Civic Space: The regional coordination of the protection strategy: By the start of the project five countries had protection mechanisms in place (Brazil, Colombia, Honduras, Mexico, and Perú). Chile and Ecuador began processes to adopt protection policies in 2023 and requested OHCHR´s technical support to assist them with advisory services throughout the process. Both governments responded affirmatively to participate in the regional meeting where the state cooperation network will be consolidated.
A systematization of the international standards from the UN system, the Inter-American Human Rights system, and tools from civil society regarding protection and access to justice for human rights defenders. This systematization aimed to familiarize states with the normative framework and assist them in their effort to develop or adapt existing protection policies to align with human rights standars.
The formal establishment of the network was expected at the first meeting on protection policies for human rights defenders co-hosted by OHCHR and ICHR, originally scheduled for November 2023 in Mexico. However, due to electoral tensions, México cancelled the event, and it was postponed to 2024, to be hosted by Colombia.
The overall progress on this pillar during 2023 has been slowed down due to the fact that the project´s general coordinator is also the civic space pillar coordinator; the general coordination role, in a project with a regional reach like this one, demands considerable dedication of time and efforts and this has been done in this case to the detriment to the allocation of time for the civic space component.
Examples of results of the second pillar in 2023 :
Human Rights of migrants:
Implementation of the Subregional Strategy for Central America and Mexico
OHCHR intensified the implementation of the sub-regional strategy on migration, monitoring and informing to relevant authorities on the human rights situation of migrants and refugees through the publication of one informative bulletins in 2023.
Enhanced monitoring, reporting, and information-sharing capacity of National Human Rights Institutions (NHRIs) in the region.
OHCHR significantly strenghtened the monitoring and reporting capacities of NHRI´s specially in Panama, where it aided in developing a tool that led to significant investigative actions into abuses agaist migrants in over 600 cases. Efforts in Costa Rica have also been impactful, supporting policy updates on migrants´access to justice in partnership with local NHRIs and the judiciary.
Commitment secured from CRM States to address discrimination and xenophobia through a regional campaign and the implementation of the #MyRightsMigrateWithMe toolkit.
The campaign reached:255,000 accounts on Instagram768,290 accounts on Facebook433,425 accounts on X (formerly Twitter)227,042 accounts on LinkedInPartnerships established with RINDHCA, youth journalist networks across the Americas, academia, civil society networks, and UN agencies to promote a narrative shift on migration.
Examples of results of the third pillar in 2023:
Right to a healthy environment:
Understanding of the right to a healthy environment:
OHCHR advanced signifincantly in understanding of the right to a healthy envirnoment in LAC among duty-bearers and rights-holders, playing a pivotal role in connecting stakeholders - States, civil society, businesses, and the UN-aligning priorities between environmental and human rights agendas, and championing a rights-based approach to environmental action in the region.
OHCHR advocated for integrating this approach into intergovernmental decisions, notably influencing the San Jose Declaration and four decisions (on pollution, climate change, biodiversity, and environmental education) adopted by the XXIII Meeting of Ministers of Environment of LAC. OHCHR provided technical assistance on constitutional, legal, judicial, and policy processes, impacting outcomes such as the Ecuadorian Constitutional Court´s decree review on environmental consultation which cited OHCHR´s technical note.
Another result is that OHCHR worked with environmental defenders, Indigenous Peoples, and Afro-descendants, promoting their inclusion in decision-making processes. A tangible outcome is the formation of a coalition of environmental defenders and community leaders in Central America and significant civil society involvement, including youth and Indigenous Peoples, in Escazú Agreement Consultations.
Progress results in 2024
The 2024 annual report has not yet been received, but during the annual meeting, OHCHR presented a preview of the results achieved so far, which are described below:
Results and impact achieved shared in the Annual Meeting
1. Promoting the expansion of civic space and the protection of human rights defenders and journalists in the LAC region.
-Consolidated regional networks for the protection of civic and social space defenders.
-Strengthened institutional capacities in the prevention and protection of human rights defenders.
-Improved capacities of prosecutors' offices in investigating attacks and murders of defenders.
-Dialogue mechanisms promoted between civil society and state actors
-Greater regional visibility on the situation of journalists and communicators.
-Technical tools developed for digital and collective protection.
-Network of civil society trainers specialized in the protection of the digital space.
-Regional action plan under way for the implementation of Article 9 of the Escazú Agreement.
2. Promoting and protecting the human rights of migrants in vulnerable situations.
-Subregional Migration Strategy for Central America and Mexico together with the Country Offices in Honduras, Guatemala and Mexico in implementation. Effective promotion and protection of human rights.
-Greater dialogue and exchange on international standards between States and civil society with universal and regional mechanisms for the protection of human rights Protocols, policies and guidelines adopted for the effective realization of the right to justice of migrants and the search and identification of missing migrants.
-Positioning of civil society in spaces for discussion and political advocacy for migration governance.
-Greater availability of information on patterns of human rights violations of migrants through border monitoring in coordination and technical support to NHRIs and NPMs.
-Changing narratives on migration with a human rights approach in partnership with journalists and digital content creators.
3. Promoting the right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment.
-Multilateral decision-making at COP 3 Escazú, COP16 CBD and SIDS4 that incorporated human rights-based approaches, with positive advocacy and technical cooperation from OHCHR. Highlights:
-Article 9 Regional Action Plan and the Modalities of Work of the Implementation and Compliance Support Committee.
-Creation of the CBD subsidiary body on Indigenous Peoples and local communities.
-National decision-making, for example, in Barbados, Brazil and Colombia, with technical cooperation from OHCHR.
-Capacity building.
-In collaboration with RINDHCA, the capacities of INDH focal points from 18 countries have been strengthened for the management of information on environmental matters and their coordination for the response to climate emergencies.
-Support for the strengthening of 7 (sub) regional coalitions on human rights and the environment.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
